item.title: Quote of the day by Bhagat Singh: ‘Study so that you are able to meet the arguments of your opponents,’ and why knowledge is the strongest answer to disagreement
item.description: In his advice, Bhagat Singh champions the importance of informed study as a tool for constructive disagreement. Engaging with significant questions thoughtfully allows for deeper discussions, moving past simplistic slogans. This intellectual approach not only makes debates more fruitful but also enhances one's ability to effect lasting change and embrace civic responsibility.
item.dc:creator: TOI News Desk

item.title: Quote of the day by Franz Kafka: ‘By believing passionately in something that still does not exist, we create it,’ and why imagination is the first step towards innovation
item.description: Innovation and change are ignited by imagination, as our belief in the unseen brings them to life. Many realities begin as mere concepts in the mind before emerging into existence. Breakthroughs frequently arise from ideas that others deem impossible, often met with skepticism. These ideas need nurturing and persistence, evolving through revision while overcoming disappointments. Our future materializes first in our dreams before it becomes a part of our reality.
item.dc:creator: TOI News Desk

item.title: Indian-American couple announces graduate fellowship for University of Texas students, says it's 'simply an open door'
item.description: Indian-American philanthropists are making significant contributions to American universities this year. Anil Kochhar and his wife Marilyn paid the education loans for graduating students at North Carolina State University. Jyoti and Nishi Bhatia established an endowment for graduate fellowships at the University of Texas. This fellowship will support students with expanded resources and financial aid. The Bhatias hope their contribution will inspire future generosity among recipients.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Quote of the day by Amal Clooney: "There is lots of my work that takes place behind closed doors that is…" – the hidden truth about dedication and lasting success
item.description: Amal Clooney highlights that much important legal work remains unseen by the public. Most of her efforts involve private meetings and extensive case preparation. This hidden groundwork forms the essential foundation for any successful outcome. The quote encourages valuing the entire process, not just the final visible result. This perspective applies broadly to many professions and their quiet dedication.

item.title: New Zealand is investing $202 million in a mega-operation aimed at restoring three islands destroyed by invasive species
item.description: In an inspiring ecological restoration project, New Zealand is teaming up with Māori natives to tackle invasive mammal populations on three major islands, including Maukahuka, Rakiura, and the Chatham archipelago. This extensive collaboration among governmental bodies, local communities, and Indigenous organizations aims to breathe new life into native wildlife. The success of this project could highlight New Zealand's pioneering methods in environmental restoration on the world stage.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Arika Kundu, 13, turns peanut shell waste into pesticide remover, competes for $25,000 prize
item.description: Thirteen-year-old Minnesota student Arika Kundu has designed a method that uses discarded peanut shells to help remove pesticide residues from fresh fruits and vegetables. Her project, called LIGNEX, has made her one of 10 finalists in the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge. She will now compete for the $25,000 grand prize with guidance from a 3M scientist.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: For centuries, scientists couldn't explain why flamingos aren't born pink until a breakthrough in the 1960s revealed the answer
item.description: Flamingos obtain their striking pink color from dietary carotenoids found in algae and brine shrimp. These pigments are converted by the birds into compounds that accumulate in their feathers. Young flamingos hatch with muted colors and gradually develop pink as they mature. Different species exhibit varying shades of pink based on their specific food sources. This coloration plays a vital role in their survival and reproductive success.

item.title: Study finds monkeys recognise shapes in ways surprisingly similar to humans
item.description: New research indicates monkeys and humans process geometric shapes similarly. This suggests geometric intuition evolved long before modern humans appeared. Rotated shapes revealed abstract reasoning abilities in monkeys and children. The study found shared cognitive mechanisms rather than separate systems. Human geometric abilities build upon primate foundations, not entirely new reasoning.

item.title: Invasive Mussels cleaned Great Lakes, but put native Whitefish at risk of vanishing forever
item.description: Invasive zebra and quagga mussels have transformed the Great Lakes ecosystem by reducing the tiny organisms that young lake whitefish depend on for food. While the mussels made the water cleaner, they disrupted the food chain, causing whitefish numbers to fall sharply. Scientists warn the species could vanish from some areas within five years.

item.title: Elon Musk's Flight 13 Starship lands successfully in the Indian Ocean; remained afloat for five days
item.description: SpaceX's Starship 40 achieved a successful splashdown landing in the Indian Ocean. The spacecraft remained intact and afloat for five days after its return. This marked a significant achievement for SpaceX's reusable rocket technology. Earlier Starship test flights experienced various failures and explosions upon landing. SpaceX is now sending a ship to recover the intact Starship 40.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Josh Allen’s charity golf event raises $17M; fatherhood deepens his empathy
item.description: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen now understands parents facing hospital crises more deeply. His daughter Harper's birth has profoundly changed his perspective on children's health struggles. Allen spoke emotionally at his "117 Holes for Charity" event, which supports Golisano Children's Hospital. This fundraiser recently helped the Patricia Allen Fund reach seventeen million dollars in donations. Fatherhood has reshaped Allen's priorities and his connection to the community.

item.title: World’s oldest near-complete Roman armour may reveal a lost soldier’s fate
item.description: Archaeologists conserved an intact Roman armour suit from the Kalkriese battlefield. This armour represents the earliest known lorica segmentata, revealing sophisticated engineering. CT scans helped uncover the armour's hidden structure without causing damage. A Roman restraint found with the armour raises questions about a captured soldier. The discovery provides a rare personal glimpse into a disastrous Roman military campaign.
